summary: Tracks indicator index of a selected tab in an ordered strip through insert, remove, and reverse operations.

traps.quote: An existing selection remains attached to the same identifier.
traps.consequence: Tracking selection as position causes wrong index after insert/remove/reverse change positions.
traps.guard: Track which identifier is selected, not its position; map to position when needed.

traps.quote: use the order immediately before this operation... select the first surviving tab to its right
traps.consequence: Cannot determine which tabs are to the right without pre-removal positions and order.
traps.guard: Record pre-removal order and positions before any removals; find survivors by original index.

traps.consequence: Wrong selection if selection rule applied after each removal instead of once at end.
traps.guard: Remove all identifiers atomically; apply selection rule once after all are removed.

traps.quote: If the strip was empty, the first inserted identifier becomes selected.
traps.consequence: Empty strip after insert remains unselected instead of selecting the first inserted ID.
traps.guard: Check if strip was empty before insert; select first inserted ID if so.

traps.quote: After every operation, append the current indicator index to the result
traps.consequence: Returning initial index as first element even with zero operations; wrong output shape.
traps.guard: Build result list only by appending after each operation; will be empty if none.

traps.consequence: Off-by-one reversal error leaves all positions wrong after reverse operation.
traps.guard: Reverse positions [left, right) with right as exclusive upper bound; use correct indexing.

input_shape: initial_ids (list of distinct int64), selected_index (int), operations (list of tuples). Max 300K total identifiers, 200K operations.
output_shape: List of integers: indicator index after each operation, or -1 if no tab selected.
invariants: Selection attaches to an identifier, not a position; remains the same identifier through all operations.
Empty strip is represented by selected_index = -1; becomes selected on first insert.
All identifiers are globally distinct; previously removed identifiers cannot be re-inserted.
max_scale: 300,000 total identifiers across initial_ids and all inserts; 200,000 operations; reverse ranges unbounded.
